decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 5.25% to 5.5%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: In recent months, there has been modest further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In recent months, there has been a lack of further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.”

changes.quote: Beginning in June, the Committee will slow the pace of decline of its securities holdings by reducing the monthly redemption cap on Treasury securities from $60 billion to $25 billion.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The Committee will maintain the monthly redemption cap on agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities at $35 billion and will reinvest any principal payments in excess of this cap into Treasury securities.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.59% APR costs about $89.96 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.31% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.03% would fall by about $16.11 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 123k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.2% over the past year (May 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -6 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.85%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.17% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 96%, cut 3%, hike 1%.

citations.detail: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
